editorial:
The Fixer Uppers is a two-reel Laurel & Hardy comedy from Hal Roach Studios, registered by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Corp. on 26 February 1935 (LP5371). Its appeal to a creator is obvious: the team's name recognition and a short that is easy to clip. The queue flagged it as a likely renewal absence, but that guess is wrong.

The 1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries lists the renewal: Hal Roach Studios, claimed as proprietor of a work made for hire, received on 1 August 1962 under R299645. Because the film was renewed on time, the copyright is still in force. Copies on the Internet Archive are uploads, not a sign that the film is free to reuse. Get a licence from the rights holder.
faq: Is The Fixer Uppers (1935) public domain in the US?
No. The 1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries lists a renewal for it (R299645, Hal Roach Studios, received 1 August 1962), so the 1935 copyright was extended. Do not treat it as free to reuse.
Does a copy on the Internet Archive mean I can reuse it?
No. A copy being hosted there says nothing about the copyright. The renewal entry controls, so reuse needs permission from whoever holds the rights.
